title: Telerehabilitation in patients with respiratory tract diseases: protocol for a scoping review

Department of Respiratory Medicine, Hyogo Prefectural Amagasaki General Medical Center, Higashinaniwa-cho 2-17-77, Amagasaki 660-8550 JAPAN Background Telerehabilitation is delivery of therapeutic rehabilitation at a distance or offs ite using telecommunication technologies. Telerehabilitation has been proposed as a health service option to enable more patients to receive rehabilitation regardless of where they live (1). Although there was some systematic review of telerehabilitation for patients with stroke (2), multiple sclerosis (3), and lower-limb joint replacement (4), telerehabilitation for respiratory diseases and respiratory infections is not known. During the COVID -19 pandemic, telerehabilitation may represent the first option for people at home (5). The COVID-19 is one of respiratory tract disease, and rapid and widespread transmission was demonstrated (6). Therefore, it is necessary consider telerehabilitation in patients with respiratory tract disease in the acute phase in hospital as well as chronic phase from the perspective of infection prevention. The purpose of this scoping review is to assess the intervention program, safety and feasibility of telerehabilitation for patients with respiratory tract diseases in the COVID-
19 era. Methods We describe this protocol that follows the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-
ScR) statement(7). We also use the scoping review framework by The Joanna Briggs Institute

(JBI) (8) following five stage approach as below. Stage 1: Identifying the research question We are interested in telerehabilitation for patients with respiratory tract disease, a nd the research questions are as followed: 1. “What is telerehabilitation for patients with respiratory tract disease?” 2. “How safe is telerehabilitation for patients with respiratory tract disease?” 3. “How feasible is telerehabilitation for patients with COVID-19?” Stage 2: Identifying relevant studies We used the Population, Concept, and Context (PCC) framework (8) to define the inclusion criteria as follows: Participants All published studies that include patients with respiratory tract disease including respiratory infection such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) coronavirus (CoV) infections, Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS) CoV and COVID-19. In this scoping review, ICD-
10 codes of the participants include J00 -J99 Diseases of the re spiratory system , A15 -16 Respiratory tuberculosis, U04 Severe acute respiratory syndrome, U07.1 COVID -19, virus identified, U07.2 COVID-19, virus not identified. Concept We will review the existing literature on telerehabilitation for patients with resp iratory tract disease regarding rehabilitation programs, feasibility and safety. Context In this review, telerehabilitation is defined as “ Delivery of therapeutic rehabilitation at a distance or offsite using telecommunication technologies”. We will also include the study for telerehabilitation, remote rehabilitation and virtual rehabilitation as defined by authors Studies in any setting (including in hospital) and phase and from any country and with any length of follow-up will be included. The following databases will be searched: MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Resister of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), CINAHL and PEDro. In addition, we will search for ongoing trials in the following trials register: the World Health Organization Intern ational Clinical Trials Registry Platform and ClinicalTraials.gov. We will also search for references in the articles identified for inclusion.

All published randomized controlled trials, crossover trials, cluster-randomized trials, quasi-
randomized trials and non-randomized trials. observational studies with control, case reports and case series will be included. Studies in any languages and from any country will be accepted, and we will include study with any length of follow-up. Abstract & Title: telerehabilitation OR “remote rehabilitation” OR “virtual rehabilitation” ClinicalTrials.gov Condition or disease: Respiratory OR COVID OR MERS OR SERS OR tuberculosis OR pulmonary Intervention: Telerehabilitation OR tele rehabilitation OR remote rehabilitation OR virtual rehabilitation Stage 3: Study selection We will select studies following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (PRISMA) flow diagram (9). We will use the PCC framework and the process will be carrie d out independently by two researchers (ST and KY). The two authors will compare their lists and any differences in opinion will be resolved by discussion and, where this fails, through arbitration by a third researcher (YK). Stage 4: Charting the data Data extraction will be carried out by one researcher (ST) using standard data extraction forms including diagnosis, setting, study type, number of participants, telerehabilitation program, control, outcomes, adverse events, and feasibility. Another one res earcher ( KY) confirm the data extraction. If necessary, we will contact the authors of these studies. Stage 5: Collating, summarizing, and reporting the results We will present the results of the search in the PRISMA flow diagram. We will organize the extracted data described above as qualitative synthesis (Table 1, Table 2).

Ethics and dissemination In this scoping review, only data from previously conducted studies will be analyzed. We will publish this scoping review in peer-reviewed journals. Patients and or public involvement Patients and or public were not involved in the development of this protocol. The study group developed this study protocol without patient involvement.
